passages.provision_quote: For the following compliance periods, the quantities shall reflect reasonable progress in each of the intervening years sufficient to ensure that the procurement of electricity products from eligible renewable energy resources achieves 25 percent of retail sales by December 31, 2016, 33 percent by December 31, 2020, 44 percent by December 31, 2024, 52 percent by December 31, 2027, and 60 percent by December 31, 2030. The commission shall establish appropriate three-year compliance periods for all subsequent years that require retail sellers to procure not less than 60 percent of retail sales of electricity products from eligible renewable energy resources.
passages.note: Chaptered text of the bill he voted for; it prints the operative procurement requirement and its dated targets but names no voter.

rows.reasoning: Gabriel voted Aye on final Assembly passage of SB 100 (2017-2018), a single-subject bill on the renewables portfolio standard whose operative sections direct that "the commission shall establish a renewables portfolio standard requiring all retail sellers to procure a minimum quantity of electricity products from eligible renewable energy resources" rising to "60 percent by December 31, 2030", enforced by penalties for noncompliance. That is a requirement carried by dated targets, matching the rung "Require a shift to clean energy through mandates and firm deadlines." The bill carries no appropriation, subsidy or tax credit and does not loosen permitting, so the funding and red-tape rungs are excluded, and the Assembly tally of 44 ayes to 33 noes is far from near-unanimous.
